profile.campus: White Oak Technology Park, Henrico County, Virginia (Meta's Henrico data center campus, near Richmond)
profile.reading:
This Meta data center building (building 1 of 3 mapped in this cluster) is part of Meta's Henrico campus at the White Oak Technology Park near Richmond, Virginia. The project was first publicly discussed as "Project Echo" in September 2017 and formally announced by Facebook that October, with Facebook committing $750 million directly and total planned investment reported at $1 billion; the first phase totaled 970,000 square feet, with potential full build-out envisioned at up to 2.5 million square feet, per Data Center Dynamics and Data Center Knowledge's contemporaneous coverage. The Henrico facility went online and began serving data in August 2020, supporting 200 long-term jobs and having drawn more than 1,500 construction workers at peak building phases. To supply renewable power, Dominion Energy Virginia created a new tariff, Schedule RF, specifically to let large customers like Facebook fund dedicated Virginia solar generation without shifting costs to other ratepayers; Facebook said it funded 500 megawatts of new Virginia solar capacity to source the Henrico center's power as 100% renewable energy, with strong political backing at the time from Governor Terry McAuliffe's administration. Meta's own current fact sheet for the campus reports LEED Gold certification and Meta's standard net-zero, 100%-renewable, and water-positive-by-2030 commitments. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact current building count, or per-building square footage beyond the original 970,000-square-foot Phase 1 figure; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

Meta has continued expanding at White Oak: in October 2022 it purchased 475 acres at 3951 Portugee Road for $35.3 million under the internal code name "Project Tropical" (following the earlier "Project Echo" naming), more than doubling its White Oak holdings to just over 800 acres, after roughly 326 acres acquired between 2017 and 2020 for about $13.4 million, according to Richmond BizSense's reporting on county planning filings. Conceptual plans filed with Henrico County called for two additional data centers and three auxiliary buildings on the wooded parcel directly south of Meta's existing facility, by then described in county filings as roughly 2.4 million square feet. Henrico's attractiveness for the expansion was tied by that reporting to the area's proximity to transatlantic subsea internet cables landing at Virginia Beach and to the county's decision to cut its data-center tax rate by about 88 percent, to 40 cents per $100 of assessed value.

profile.capacity_note: Meta does not publish per-building IT capacity or a confirmed current building count for Henrico; Phase 1 was reported at 970,000 square feet, with potential full build-out cited at up to 2.5 million square feet. No confirmed current per-building figure is asserted here.

profile.research_note: Cowork facility-page writer, 2026-09-03: rebuilt from a 2026-09-02 pass that had exhausted its WebSearch budget and left the row with only generic company-level Wikipedia narration and no reading/facility_note/regional_context/capacity_note in the compliant schema. Fresh research this session used Meta's own Henrico fact sheet (tier-1), DCD's August 2020 activation report (tier-2, confirms year_opened=2020 and Phase 1 sqft), and Data Center Knowledge's 2017 reporting on the Dominion Energy Schedule RF renewable tariff created specifically for this project (tier-2, contemporaneous utility-regulatory coverage). Fact-box expected at 4 of 8 (address, campus, year_opened, technical_space_sqft), an improvement over the pure 2-key gap at several other Meta campuses this session because DCD/DCK reporting supplied a genuine Phase 1 square-footage figure and confirmed activation year.
profile.regional_context: Henrico County sits just outside Richmond and is part of Virginia's broader data-center growth beyond the dominant Northern Virginia/Loudoun County cluster; Dominion Energy's Schedule RF tariff created for this Facebook project was cited at the time as a model that other major data-center operators active in Virginia, including AWS, Equinix, and Digital Realty, could potentially use for their own renewable-energy commitments.

reading.body:
Meta owns and operates a data center campus in Henrico County, Virginia, but the operator has not published power capacity, building count, square footage, or opening date for this facility. The research status is exhausted, and independent confirmation of site-specific details was not available in this session. Virginia hosts 326 mapped data center facilities, of which 23 publish power consumption figures totaling 1,375 megawatts, but this campus does not appear among them.

Without published specifications, this facility cannot be ranked by size or load within Virginia's portfolio or assessed for its role in the state's AI infrastructure. The campus sits in a state where published capacity is concentrated in a small fraction of mapped sites, a pattern consistent with most data center locations remaining opaque to public scrutiny. The absence of published figures does not indicate the facility is small or dormant; it indicates the operator has chosen not to disclose this information.

For readers evaluating whether this campus matters to AI, the lack of published data means it cannot be weighed against other sites in capacity planning, grid impact assessment, or supply chain analysis. To determine whether Meta's Henrico investment affects AI scaling constraints, direct inquiry of the operator or discovery of internal filings would be required.
